headline: Kentucky turns windy and colder behind today's front; the Upstate stays warm through afternoon before a sharp, mostly dry weekend cool-down
disclaimer: Independent amateur analysis. This is not an official forecast or warning. Follow the National Weather Service and local authorities during hazardous weather.

refresh.workflow: Update and commit forecast.json once. GitHub Actions automatically locks the prior issue in forecast-history.json. Then verify the GitHub Pages URL; every Google Sites embed reads the same file and refreshes automatically.

kentucky.name: Central Kentucky
kentucky.subtitle: Danville primary · Lexington comparison
kentucky.summary: The cold front has crossed Central Kentucky. Scattered light showers, gusty northwest winds and falling temperatures continue through late afternoon, followed by stubborn clouds tonight. Saturday is brisk and much cooler. Clearing Saturday night creates a strong frost signal and a localized freeze risk Sunday morning. Sunday is sunny and somewhat milder, though another chilly night follows.

currentConditions.wind: Northwest near 14 mph, gusting to 23 mph

days.label: Friday
days.hazard: No official NWS alert at issuance. Independent concerns are northwest gusts around 20–30 mph, scattered light showers and a rapid temperature fall.
days.forecast: The day's highest temperature occurred near or before the frontal passage. Cloudy skies, scattered light showers and gusty northwest winds continue this afternoon while readings fall through the lower 60s and upper 50s. Rainfall should remain under one-tenth inch for most locations. Showers end by evening, but low clouds may persist tonight as temperatures fall into the lower 40s in many locations.

days.label: Saturday
days.hazard: No official NWS alert at issuance. Independent concerns are brisk north winds during the day and widespread frost with a localized freeze Saturday night.
days.forecast: Morning clouds give way to increasing sunshine, but a north wind keeps the day chilly. Gusts around 20–28 mph remain possible before easing late. Clearer skies and diminishing wind Saturday night favor widespread frost; rural valleys and other cold pockets may reach freezing.

days.label: Sunday
days.hazard: No official NWS alert at issuance. Independent concern is frost early Sunday, with another patchy frost risk late Sunday night in colder rural locations.
days.forecast: Areas of frost early, then sunny and somewhat milder as high pressure settles over the region. East winds remain light. Clear skies Sunday night allow another chilly period, although most locations should remain above freezing.

kentucky.bottomLine: Kentucky's warm spell is over. Light showers, gusty northwest winds and falling temperatures continue today. Saturday is dry, brisk and cool, followed by widespread frost and a localized freeze Saturday night. Sunday is sunny and somewhat milder.
kentucky.confidence: High on the cool-down, dry weekend and frost potential; moderate-high on today's shower coverage and peak gusts

upstate.name: Upstate South Carolina
upstate.subtitle: Clemson primary · Pickens County comparison
upstate.summary: Morning fog has cleared around Clemson and Central, leaving a sunny and unusually warm afternoon ahead of the front. The front crosses this evening with little rain but an increasing west-to-northwest wind. Saturday and Sunday are sharply cooler, breezy and mostly sunny. The strongest freeze risk remains in the North Carolina mountains, while Clemson-area lows should generally remain in the upper 30s and 40s.

days.label: Friday
days.hazard: No official NWS alert at issuance. Independent concern is a gusty west-to-northwest wind shift this evening and tonight; morning fog has already cleared.
days.forecast: Sunny and very warm this afternoon, with temperatures approaching record territory at the warmer reporting sites. The front crosses during the evening with little moisture. Winds turn west to northwest and strengthen, with gusts around 20–30 mph possible overnight as temperatures fall rapidly.

days.label: Saturday
days.precipitation: 5–15% during the morning, then 5% or less
days.hazard: No official NWS alert at issuance. Independent concern is north-to-northwest gusts around 20–30 mph and much cooler temperatures.
days.forecast: A brief light shower is possible during the morning as the upper disturbance passes, but Clemson and Central should remain predominantly dry. Skies become mostly sunny while north winds stay gusty. Saturday night is clear and chilly; patchy frost is most plausible in colder sheltered locations north and west of Clemson.

days.label: Sunday
days.hazard: No official NWS alert at issuance. No significant weather hazard is expected in Clemson or Central; frost remains more likely in the mountains and colder northern foothills.
days.forecast: Sunny, cool and breezy with a northeast wind. Temperatures remain well below Friday's warmth. Sunday night is mostly clear and chilly, but widespread frost or freezing temperatures are not expected in the Clemson–Central corridor.

upstate.bottomLine: One more warm, sunny afternoon precedes a mostly dry frontal passage this evening. Gusty winds and a 20-degree cool-down follow. Saturday and Sunday are breezy, mostly sunny and much cooler, while the greatest freeze risk stays in the mountains.
upstate.confidence: High on today's warmth and the weekend cool-down; moderate-high on frontal wind timing; moderate on the small Saturday-morning shower chance

sourceNotes: No official NWS watch, warning or advisory was active for either configured regional point at 11:25 AM EDT on October 16, 2026.

The NWS /points service was re-resolved at analysis time. Danville maps to LMK/86,53 and Clemson maps to GSP/49,34. Earlier stored links LMK/83,54 and GSP/40,55 did not represent the configured coordinates and were excluded from this candidate.

College of DuPage radar at 11:20 AM EDT showed scattered light returns in and near Kentucky, while the Upstate remained dry. True-color satellite at 11:16 AM showed the frontal cloud band over the Ohio/Tennessee Valleys and much clearer skies across the Carolinas.
Official point forecasts, current observations, office discussions and multi-model guidance are consistent after correcting the point URLs; no unresolved material source conflict remains.
HRRR, RAP, NAM, NAM 3-km Nest, GFS, GEFS and ECMWF availability was verified from official run directories; College of DuPage panels supplied a common visual source.
Tempest data was not used for Upstate observations, verification, calibration or adjustment.
Official NWS alerts are separate from this independent analysis. Independent hazard probabilities do not constitute watches or warnings.
